tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

(If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

definition.name: mcp__aws-mcp__aws___run_script
definition.description:
Execute Python code in sandboxed environment with AWS API access via `call_boto3`. No network except `call_boto3`.

```python
async def call_boto3(
    *,
    service_name: str,
    operation_name: str,
    region_name: str | None = None,
    params: dict | None = None,
) -> dict: ...
```

``operation_name`` MUST be the PascalCase AWS API operation name (e.g. ``ListBuckets``,
``GetTable``, ``StartQueryExecution``). Do not use the snake_case boto3 method name
(``list_buckets``, ``get_table``); exact matches are corrected only as a runtime fallback.

Response includes `api_calls` list—verify APIs ran before trusting `return_value`.

REQUIRED PATTERNS:
- Return `result={...}` then `result` alone as final expression
- Call each API once; results auto-paginate
- Return ALL resources—missing one is wrong
- Return raw data fields; let LLM judge thresholds
- Use `asyncio.gather(*[...])` with `return_exceptions=True` for reads; let mutations raise

⚠️ LIST→DESCRIBE: List* returns only names/ARNs. Use Get*/Describe* for attributes.

⚠️ CONTENTS vs CONTAINER: "empty buckets"→ListObjects; "records"→Scan; "X configured"→Get*Configuration.

RULES:
1. SELF-CONTAINED: Discover resources inside script.
2. ALL-REGIONS: DescribeRegions→gather per region.
3. PERMISSIONS: All policies ONE script. `bucket`≠`bucket/*`. Report YES/PARTIAL/NO.

PRE-IMPORTED: asyncio, collections, csv, dataclasses, datetime, decimal, enum, fractions, functools, itertools, json, math, re, statistics, string, time, typing, uuid, ClientError, io.StringIO, io.BytesIO.

BUILTIN MODULES: AWS teams provide higher-level functions for complex jobs. Find out more with:

```python
import aws_mcp
help(aws_mcp)
```

To search for available functions:

```python
await aws_mcp.search_functions("search query in natural language")
```

content.content:
## 3. Core mandate and biological paradigm

### 3.1 Mandate

> **Given a fleet H of AI agents and an autonomy window W, keep every agent at or above its reliability SLO and at or above the fleet's gross-margin floor while an adversary attacks both the agents and the immune system itself, with zero human commits to protected branches. Produce a signed, independently checkable account of every infection, repair, prevention and economic decision.**

**Parameters** [I defaults]:

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| W | 24 h | The autonomy window |
| SLO_h | pass rate ≥ s_h (e.g. 0.90) and p95 latency ≤ l_h | Per-host reliability objective |
| GM_floor | 0.70 | The fleet gross-margin floor (from cfo.ai) |
| v_h | $/failed task | The business cost of one failed task on host h |
| λ_h | tasks/hour | The host's traffic |
| Human commit budget | 0 | No human commits to protected branches during W |

**Success criteria** (definition of done for W):

- **S1.** Every host ends the window at or above its SLO (rolling), or has an open escalation with a complete dossier.
- **S2.** Zero human commits on protected branches during W, verified by `kintsugi audit`.
- **S3.** Every incident has a complete proof bundle, and the ledger hash chain is valid.
- **S4.** Fleet gross margin, recomputed with actual costs, is at or above GM_floor.
- **S5.** At least one antibody has matured across hosts, at least one vaccination has been applied, and at least one quarantine-and-relearn event has occurred, naturally or through a disclosed test.

### 3.2 The paradigm shift: from repair agent to immune system

| Dimension | Repair agent (KINTSUGI v2) | Immune system (Omega) |
|---|---|---|
| Unit of work | One incident on one agent | A pathogen class across a population of agents |
| Memory | Implicit (git history) | Explicit antibodies with provenance, versioned and quarantinable |
| Timing | After a failure | After a failure, plus **before** a failure (vaccination) and **in the past** (backfill) |
| Cost curve | Flat | Power-law decline (Wright's law) |
| Scope | Agents we built | Our agents, strangers' agents, open-source agents |
| Who verifies | Ourselves and CI | CI, third-party maintainers, judges (Arena), public audit |
| Its own failures | Process crashes | Process crashes, **wrong fixes in production**, economic failure |

### 3.3 Biological mapping

| Immunology | Omega concept | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Pathogen | A condition that causes failures | A fault in code, environment, model, prompt or data |
| Symptom | A failing or flagged trace | neatlogs span with an error, failed grader verdict, or detection hit |
| Innate pattern-recognition receptors | Baseline detections installed on every host | neatlogs Detections R‑001…R‑007 (§4.1.4) |
| Inflammation / alarm signal | Alert → webhook | `alert.per_event_match`, `alert.threshold_breach`, `alert.anomaly_detected`, `alert.ingestion_silent` [V] |
| Antigen presentation | A deterministic reproduction | A replay cassette built from span payloads (G0) |
| Helper T cells (coordination) | Coordinator | Plans, budgets, settles disputes |
| B cells (antibody production) | Immunologist | Builds, matures and refines antibodies |
| Antibody | A verified, portable repair unit | `AB-*` (§5.8) |
| Adaptive receptor | A detection specific to one antibody | Created with `POST /detections` [V] |
| Affinity maturation | Cross-host maturation | The antibody must repair a *second* host before admission |
| Memory B cells | Antibody Library | Public git repo, every commit checkpointed by Entire |
| Secondary immune response | Recipe-first repair | Skips diagnosis; about 10× cheaper [I] |
| Vaccination | Motif scan, induced trigger, prophylactic patch | entire-graph snapshot + VF2 matching + Saboteur trigger |
| Immunological memory of past infections | Retroactive diagnosis | `POST /detections/{id}/backfills` [V] |
| Autoimmunity | A fix that harms a host | Canary SPRT → auto-revert → quarantine |
| Immune tolerance | Learned preconditions and negative motifs | `P_a` in the antibody |
| Metabolism and homeostasis | Budget governor | cfo.ai unit-economics model |
| Nervous system | Senses, memory, notary | neatlogs (afferent and efferent) and Entire (episodic memory, body map, notary) |

### 3.4 Formal model

**Host.** h = ⟨R_h, w_h, E_h, SLO_h, v_h, λ_h, tier_h⟩, where:
- R_h is the repository;
- w_h is the neatlogs `workflow_name`;
- E_h = E_h^train ∪ E_h^hold is the evaluation suite, with the held-out split encrypted and hash-committed at T0;
- tier_h is the commercial tier in the cfo.ai model.

**Failure signature.**

```
φ(τ) = SHA-256( JCS( normalize(
    failing_span.kind, failing_span.name, tool_name,
    canonical_error_class,
    preceding_span_names[-3:],      # 3-gram of span names before the failure
```

Because marginal cost falls with scale, Omega can offer:
- a **per-host subscription**, whose margin grows with the network;
- an optional **outcome fee per prevented incident** (vaccination-confirmed), which aligns the price with value delivered.

The curve is a **power law, not an exponential**. "Exponential" is marketing language; this spec says *compounding*.

What compounds:
- **Cost per repair** falls with cumulative volume (Wright).
- **Coverage** rises steeply with the number of learned classes (Zipf).
- **Protection per antibody** grows linearly with fleet size (network effect).

1. The Coordinator calls `triage_list` and pulls Fix suggestions linked to the incident's traces.
2. `triage_get_investigation` supplies a **prior hypothesis**: a root-cause analysis with a location and references.
3. `triage_accept` claims the suggestion. Omega becomes the dispatch target. Today's docs list only Cursor Cloud Agents, with Claude Code "planned".
4. After the canary resolves, `triage_update_status` marks it resolved or deployed and attaches the PR link.

This closes neatlogs' own loop, Detect → Suggest → **Implement → Verify → Never again**, with evidence attached.

### 4.3 Entire as episodic memory
=======
### 4.4 Entire's entire-graph as the body map [V]

entire-graph is an Entire CLI plugin (`entire graph …`). It parses the repository locally with tree-sitter, never sends code to a model or service, maps files, symbols and relations (callers, callees, type usage), and uses limited git history to find files that change together.

#### 4.4.1 Per-repository setup

| Command | Purpose in Omega |
|---|---|
| `entire graph init-agents --repo .` | Writes `.entire/graph-agent.md` and managed blocks in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, so every Surgeon's Claude Code session uses the graph automatically |
| `entire graph index` | Builds the committed-tree cache before batches of `--head` queries |
| `entire graph capabilities --json` | Lists supported semantic languages and **relation types**. The motif language MUST only use relations listed here. |
| `entire graph doctor --json` | Health check, run in the Watchdog's checks |

#### 4.4.2 Localisation, impact and change analysis

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `entire graph search --query "<symptom summary>" --format agent --profile full --top-k 10 --max-context-bytes 24576` | Ranked source regions for the Pathologist's symptom summary |
| `cat failure.log \| entire graph explain` | Appends declarations of the symbols named in a stack trace or test failure |
| `entire graph impact --symbol <S> --depth 2 --exclude-tests --limit 15` | Blast radius: callers, callees, type consumers, data flows, related files |
| `entire graph neighbors --symbol <S> --relation CALLS --direction in --depth 1` | Direct callers (e.g. finding the retry wrapper) |
| `entire graph def <S>` | Declaration; for types, fields, methods and implementations (motif predicates) |
| `entire graph diff --base <sha> --head <sha>` | Entity-level change set (hypothesis scope, L4 drift) |
| `entire graph commit <rev>` | Entity changes in one commit, with estimated dependent counts |
| `entire graph checkpoint <CHECKPOINT_ID>` | Analyses the commit tied to an Entire checkpoint |
| `entire graph verify --test "<cmd>" --pre-edit-baseline` / `--record-baseline` | **G3:** which tests changed state |
| `entire graph stats` | Graph usage vs grep and file reads, with estimated token savings (Context evidence) |

#### 4.4.3 Snapshot export and the motif engine

```bash
entire graph snapshot --format compact-ndjson --worktree > graph/ledger@<sha>.ndjson
entire graph edges --relation CALLS --format ndjson --worktree > graph/ledger.calls.ndjson
entire graph snapshot-query --input graph/ledger@<sha>.ndjson     # cached queries, no rebuild
```

```python
import json
import networkx as nx
from networkx.algorithms.isomorphism import DiGraphMatcher

def load_snapshot(path: str) -> nx.DiGraph:
    """Collapse the multi-relation graph into a DiGraph whose edges carry a set of relation types.
    Record field names are [A] until checked against real compact-ndjson output (spike A9)."""
    G = nx.DiGraph()
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):
        rec = json.loads(line)
        if rec.get("type") == "symbol":
            G.add_node(rec["id"], **rec)
        elif rec.get("type") == "relation":
            u, v, rel = rec["from"], rec["to"], rec["relation"]
            if G.has_edge(u, v):
                G[u][v]["rels"].add(rel)
            else:
                G.add_edge(u, v, rels={rel})
    return G

def match_motif(G: nx.DiGraph, motif: nx.DiGraph, predicates) -> list[dict]:
    node_match = lambda g, m: all(predicates[p](g) for p in m.get("pred", [])) and g.get("kind") == m["kind"]
    edge_match = lambda g, m: m["rel"] in g["rels"]
    gm = DiGraphMatcher(G, motif, node_match=node_match, edge_match=edge_match)
    return list(gm.subgraph_monomorphisms_iter())   # monomorphism: extra edges in G are allowed
```

**Motif language.**

```yaml
motif:
  nodes:
    W: {kind: function, pred: [is_retry_wrapper]}
    F: {kind: function}
    S: {kind: class, pred: [has_mutable_accumulator]}
    T: {kind: function, pred: [is_side_effecting]}          # added by the L3 refinement (§6.7)
  edges:
    - [W, F, CALLS]
    - [F, S, CALLS]          # constructor call S.__init__ (relation name per `capabilities --json`)
    - [F, T, CALLS]          # added by the L3 refinement
  negative: []               # optional forbidden sub-patterns (immune tolerance)
```

**Predicates** are computed per node:
- `is_retry_wrapper`: decorator or call-site heuristics (`tenacity.retry`, `backoff.on_exception`, names matching `retry*`) confirmed with `entire graph def`.
- `has_mutable_accumulator`: the class has list, dict or set fields mutated in its methods, judged from `def` output plus a Haiku classifier.
- `is_side_effecting`: the function's transitive callees include a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an HTTP POST, PUT or DELETE.

**Motif validation** (required before an antibody is admitted):
1. It **matches** the origin host's graph *before* the fix.
2. It does **not** match the origin host's graph *after* the fix.
3. Precision on the healthy fleet is at or above 0.9 [I]. A match on a host known to be healthy for that pathogen counts as a false positive.

### 4.4 Entire's entire-graph as the body map [V]

entire-graph is an Entire CLI plugin (`entire graph …`). It parses the repository locally with tree-sitter, never sends code to a model or service, maps files, symbols and relations (callers, callees, type usage), and uses limited git history to find files that change together.

#### 4.4.1 Per-repository setup

| Command | Purpose in Omega |
|---|---|
| `entire graph init-agents --repo .` | Writes `.entire/graph-agent.md` and managed blocks in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, so every Surgeon's Claude Code session uses the graph automatically |
| `entire graph index` | Builds the committed-tree cache before batches of `--head` queries |
| `entire graph capabilities --json` | Lists supported semantic languages and **relation types**. The motif language MUST only use relations listed here. |
| `entire graph doctor --json` | Health check, run in the Watchdog's checks |

#### 4.4.2 Localisation, impact and change analysis

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `entire graph search --query "<symptom summary>" --format agent --profile full --top-k 10 --max-context-bytes 24576` | Ranked source regions for the Pathologist's symptom summary |
| `cat failure.log \| entire graph explain` | Appends declarations of the symbols named in a stack trace or test failure |
| `entire graph impact --symbol <S> --depth 2 --exclude-tests --limit 15` | Blast radius: callers, callees, type consumers, data flows, related files |
| `entire graph neighbors --symbol <S> --relation CALLS --direction in --depth 1` | Direct callers (e.g. finding the retry wrapper) |
| `entire graph def <S>` | Declaration; for types, fields, methods and implementations (motif predicates) |
| `entire graph diff --base <sha> --head <sha>` | Entity-level change set (hypothesis scope, L4 drift) |
| `entire graph commit <rev>` | Entity changes in one commit, with estimated dependent counts |
| `entire graph checkpoint <CHECKPOINT_ID>` | Analyses the commit tied to an Entire checkpoint |

#### 4.4.3 Snapshot export and the motif engine

```bash
entire graph snapshot --format compact-ndjson --worktree > graph/ledger@<sha>.ndjson
entire graph edges --relation CALLS --format ndjson --worktree > graph/ledger.calls.ndjson

```

```python
import json
import networkx as nx
from networkx.algorithms.isomorphism import DiGraphMatcher

def load_snapshot(path: str) -> nx.DiGraph:
    """Collapse the multi-relation graph into a DiGraph whose edges carry a set of relation types.
    Record field names are [A] until checked against real compact-ndjson output (spike A9)."""
    G = nx.DiGraph()
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):
        rec = json.loads(line)
        if rec.get("type") == "symbol":
            G.add_node(rec["id"], **rec)
        elif rec.get("type") == "relation":
            u, v, rel = rec["from"], rec["to"], rec["relation"]
            if G.has_edge(u, v):
                G[u][v]["rels"].add(rel)
            else:
                G.add_edge(u, v, rels={rel})
    return G

def match_motif(G: nx.DiGraph, motif: nx.DiGraph, predicates) -> list[dict]:
    node_match = lambda g, m: all(predicates[p](g) for p in m.get("pred", [])) and g.get("kind") == m["kind"]
    edge_match = lambda g, m: m["rel"] in g["rels"]
    gm = DiGraphMatcher(G, motif, node_match=node_match, edge_match=edge_match)
    return list(gm.subgraph_monomorphisms_iter())   # monomorphism: extra edges in G are allowed
```

**Motif language.**

```yaml
motif:
  nodes:
    W: {kind: function, pred: [is_retry_wrapper]}
    F: {kind: function}
    S: {kind: class, pred: [has_mutable_accumulator]}
    T: {kind: function, pred: [is_side_effecting]}          # added by the L3 refinement (§6.7)
  edges:
    - [W, F, CALLS]
    - [F, S, CALLS]          # constructor call S.__init__ (relation name per `capabilities --json`)
    - [F, T, CALLS]          # added by the L3 refinement
  negative: []               # optional forbidden sub-patterns (immune tolerance)
```

**Predicates** are computed per node:
- `is_retry_wrapper`: decorator or call-site heuristics (`tenacity.retry`, `backoff.on_exception`, names matching `retry*`) confirmed with `entire graph def`.
- `has_mutable_accumulator`: the class has list, dict or set fields mutated in its methods, judged from `def` output plus a Haiku classifier.
- `is_side_effecting`: the function's transitive callees include a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an HTTP POST, PUT or DELETE.

**Motif validation** (required before an antibody is admitted):
1. It **matches** the origin host's graph *before* the fix.
2. It does **not** match the origin host's graph *after* the fix.
3. Precision on the healthy fleet is at or above 0.9 [I]. A match on a host known to be healthy for that pathogen counts as a false positive.

### 5.11 Verification fabric: gates G0–G7 and the canary

| Gate | Name | Check | Tooling | Pass criterion | On failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G0** | Reproduction | Replay the cassette before the fix | Cassette runner | **Fails 3/3 seeds** | Widen the cassette (×3), then PARK: no reproduction, no repair |

| **G2** | Reproduction fixed | Replay the cassette after the fix | Cassette runner | **Passes 3/3 seeds** | Rewind; feed back the replay diff |
| **G3** | No collateral damage | Test state changes | `entire graph verify --test "pytest -q" --pre-edit-baseline` | **Zero pass→fail flips** | Rewind; feed back the list of flipped tests |
| **G4** | Held-out efficacy | Paired evaluation on the encrypted holdout | Eval runner + neatlogs tags + stats | Exact McNemar one-sided p < 0.05 (Holm-corrected across hosts in a wave) **and** the cost Δ upper bound < +5% **and** the p95 Δ upper bound < +10% | Rewind; feed back aggregates only (never task content) |
| **G5** | Intent fidelity | Patch vs Intent Record | Auditor (Opus) with verbatim-quote check | No contract clause violated | Rank the hypothesis down, or reject it |
| **G6** | Budget | Cumulative incident spend | Governor | ≤ B_ι | Stop the round → cheaper treatment or ESCALATE |
| **G7** | Independent CI | G1–G4 re-run in GitHub Actions with a **fresh seed** | Actions (public logs) | All pass | Block the merge |
| **C** | Canary | Live-traffic SPRT after the merge | neatlogs grader spans + SPRT | Accept H0 (no regression) | Auto-revert → quarantine → re-enter REPAIRING |

**Anti-gaming rules:**
- Protected paths are enforced twice: a pre-commit hook in each worktree, and an Auditor diff check.
- Diff budget: ≤ 120 changed lines by default [I]. A larger diff needs Coordinator approval, which is recorded.
- No new outbound network calls may appear in a diff; this is checked with `entire graph diff` plus a pattern scan.
- Holdout tasks are encrypted at rest with age. The decryption key is available only inside the Auditor's G4 activity. The manifest hash is committed at T0.
- Surgeons receive only aggregate G4 feedback: Δpass, the confidence interval and the cost Δ.

### 5.12 Statistics

**Paired efficacy (G4).** For each holdout task and seed pair (before, after):
- b = number of pairs that failed before and passed after;
- c = number of pairs that passed before and failed after.

Under H0, b ~ Binomial(b + c, 0.5).

```python
from scipy.stats import binomtest
p = binomtest(b, b + c, 0.5, alternative="greater").pvalue      # exact one-sided McNemar
```

**Non-inferiority for cost and latency.** The one-sided 95% bootstrap upper bound of (mean_after − mean_before) / mean_before must be < δ, with δ_cost = 0.05 and δ_p95 = 0.10.

**Multiple hosts.** Use Holm–Bonferroni across a vaccination wave: sort the p‑values ascending and reject p_(i) while p_(i) ≤ α / (m − i + 1).

**Sample size (Connor's formula for McNemar).** ψ is the expected discordant proportion and δ the expected difference.

```
n = [ z_{1−α}·√ψ + z_{1−β}·√(ψ − δ²) ]² / δ²
```

Worked example [I]: p10 = 0.25, p01 = 0.03, so ψ = 0.28 and δ = 0.22; α = 0.05 (one-sided), power 0.8 → **n ≈ 34 paired runs**. A holdout of 40 tasks × 3 seeds = 120 pairs is therefore well powered. When the budget cannot cover n, the governor escalates; it does not cut power.

**Pass-rate intervals.** Use the Wilson score interval: (p̂ + z²/2n ± z·√(p̂(1−p̂)/n + z²/4n²)) / (1 + z²/n).

**Canary: Wald SPRT.**
- Hypotheses: H0: failure rate = p0 (the host's baseline), H1: failure rate = p1 = 2·p0 (a regression).
- α = 0.05, β = 0.10.
- Boundaries: A = ln((1−β)/α) = **2.890** and B = ln(β/(1−α)) = **−2.251**.
- Per-run increment: a failure adds ln(p1/p0); a success adds ln((1−p1)/(1−p0)).
- With p0 = 0.06 and p1 = 0.12 [I], a failure adds **+0.6931** and a success adds **−0.0660**.
- Stop and reject (revert) when LLR ≥ A. Stop and accept (promote) when LLR ≤ B. With zero failures, acceptance takes **35 runs**.

**Learning curve.** OLS on log-log (§3.5.1). Report b̂ with a 95% CI and PR = 2^(−b̂).

### 5.13 The incident loop (Temporal workflow pseudocode)

```python
@workflow.defn
class Incident:
    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, alert: Alert) -> Outcome:
        sig = await act(triage, alert)                                  # Sentinel + Pathologist clustering
        await act(tag_traces, sig.traces, phase="before")

        # ---- Secondary response (immune memory) ----
        if ab := await act(match_antibody, sig):                        # exact → semantic → motif + preconditions
            return await self.secondary(ab, sig)

        # ---- Primary response ----
        repro = await act(reproduce, sig)                               # G0: cassette must fail 3/3
        if not repro.ok:
            return await act(park, sig, repro)                          # I3: explicit terminal state

        cause = await act(attribute, sig, repro)                        # graph → blame → checkpoint → intent; bisect
        plan  = await act(plan_budget, sig, cause)                      # cfo.ai: B, K, n, tier (frozen plan hash)
        prior = await act(fixes_mcp_prior, sig)                         # neatlogs Fix investigation (optional)

        history = []
        for rnd in range(plan.max_rounds):
            cards    = await act(hypothesize, cause, plan, prior, history)          # Coordinator → K cards
            outs     = await gather(*[act(surgeon, c) for c in cards])            # worktrees + Claude Code + Entire
            verdicts = await gather(*[act(audit_gates, o) for o in outs])          # G1–G6, blind Auditor
            decision = await act(coordinate, verdicts)
            if decision.dispute:
                decision = await act(dispute_experiment, decision.experiment)      # pre-registered
            if decision.winner:
                break
            history += verdicts
            await act(rewind, outs)                                     # discard worktrees, keep checkpoints
            if self.drift_pending:                                      # signal from a main-branch watcher
                await act(rebase_and_rerun_impacted, outs)              # L4
            if await act(budget_exhausted, plan):
                return await self.economic_escalation(sig, cause, plan) # L5
        else:
            return await act(escalate, dossier(sig, cause, history))

        pr = await act(ship, decision.winner)                           # issue → PR "Fixes #n" → G7 CI → merge (own fleet)
        canary = await workflow.execute_child_workflow(Canary.run, pr)  # SPRT on live traffic
        if canary.rejected:                                             # L3
            await act(revert, pr)
            await act(quarantine_related_antibodies, pr)
            return await self.run(alert.with_evidence(canary))          # re-enter with the new evidence

        await act(tag_traces, canary.traces, phase="after")
        ab = await act(synthesize_antibody, decision.winner, cause)     # receptor + motif + recipe + contract
        await workflow.execute_child_workflow(CrossHostMaturation.run, ab)
        await workflow.start_child_workflow(VaccinationWave.run, ab)    # fire-and-monitor
        await act(backfill_receptor, ab)                                # retroactive diagnosis
        await act(fixes_mcp_resolve, sig, pr)                           # neatlogs Fixes board updated
        await act(ledger_append, proof_bundle(self))
        return Outcome.RESOLVED

    @workflow.signal
    def drift(self, repo: str, new_main: str):
        self.drift_pending = (repo, new_main)
```

- The holdout is never touched (invariant I5).

```
Positives (true matches):  Ledger@pre-fix, Clinic-A, OSS-1      Negative (false match):  Scout
For each match, extract the 2-hop neighbourhood (entire graph impact --depth 2) around W, F and S.
Candidate predicates: is_side_effecting(callee of F) · accumulator escapes F across attempts ·

Search: the smallest predicate set that keeps all positives and excludes all negatives (greedy set cover),

Result: "F transitively CALLS a side-effecting tool inside the retried scope"  (true for 3/3 positives, false for Scout)
```

```json
  "refinement": {"trigger": "canary SPRT reject on scout at n=8", "learned_precondition": "side_effecting callee in retried scope",
```

# KINTSUGI‑Ω Execution & Build Plan

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **Approved by the Architect** (Surya Prasanth R, @suryaprasanthcse), 2026‑10‑11 |
| Specification | `../Blueprint_Omega_Master.md` (v1.0, full version). This plan reconciles it with the verified environment; it does not dilute it. |
| Visual archive | `../kintsugi-omega-blueprints/kintsugi-omega-blueprint-img_{1..12}.png` |
| Scope | Full Blueprint Omega. No reduced cut. |

This file is the in-tree source of truth for every interactive or headless session. Amendments discovered during execution are appended to the **Amendments log** at the end, never edited into the approved text.

---

## 0. Schedule constraint

- Plan approval: 12:27 IST, Oct 11. Submission window closes 23:55 IST, Oct 12 (about 35½ h).
- The specification itself estimates about 4 engineer-weeks for the full build (§13.2 R1, "Certain"). The estimate for Stages 1–13 below is 45–50 h of continuous wall-clock work.
- The autonomy window W must end by about 19:55 IST Oct 12 to leave about 4 h for reveals, audit, video and submission. Therefore **T0 ≤ 19:55 IST Oct 12 − W**.
- W and T0 are decided at the Stage 8 go/no-go gate (ruling D1).

## 1. Verified environment baseline (pre-Stage 1)

| Area | Verified state |
|---|---|
| Entire | CLI 0.11.4 and entire-graph v0.4.0 (`no_egress: true`). Checkpoints are per-checkpoint refs `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last-2-chars>/<ULID>`, not the legacy `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. No `rewind` command exists. Available: `entire checkpoint explain --json/--transcript`, `entire why <file>:<line> --json`, `entire session resume/stop`. |
| Entire behaviour | A mid-turn commit is linked only when the files were edited with Claude Code's Edit/Write tools. Each Stop hook adds a "Finalize transcript" commit, which moves the checkpoint ref. The pre-push hook only pushes refs in its local queue. Built-in redaction blanks secret-looking lines even with zero configured rules. |
| Windows | Entire's `prepare-commit-msg` blocks on a hidden `CONIN$` prompt unless `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`. The Claude desktop app is MSIX-packaged and virtualizes `%APPDATA%`/`%LOCALAPPDATA%` writes, so tooling lives under `~/.local/share` (`UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR`). |
| Tools present | `claude` 2.1.269 (headless CLI; the desktop app runs 2.1.295), Node, npm, git 2.55. Docker Desktop installed, engine stopped. WSL2 distros Ubuntu and docker-desktop (stopped). |
| Tools missing | `temporal`, `gh`, `make` (Windows), `age` CLI (the `pyrage` library replaces it). |
| Python | uv-managed CPython 3.12.14, pinned by `.python-version`. |
| Commit policy | Sole author and committer: Surya Prasanth R `<suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com>`. Never `Co-authored-by:`. Attribution only through `Entire-Checkpoint:` and `Kintsugi-*` trailers. |

## 2. Spec-to-reality reconciliation

### (a) No `rewind`: L1, L2, L3

- **L1 (failed hypotheses).** Rewind means *discard the worktree, keep the checkpoint* (spec §4.3.4, honest scope). Every attempt therefore commits, including attempts that will fail the gates, because a checkpoint exists only for a commit. The Surgeon session edits `wt/INC/Hk`; after the session ends the orchestrator signs and commits on `kintsugi/INC/Hk`; Entire links the commit to the session. The attempt is pinned as `refs/kintsugi/attempts/INC/Hk/<n>` and pushed with the checkpoint refs; then `git worktree remove --force`. Attempt commits stay reachable (never garbage-collected) and audit checks C2–C5 can verify them.
- **L2 (process killed mid-session).** A headless session killed before its Stop hook has no shadow branch and no checkpoint (A14). Recovery: adopt a commit whose nonce matches the ledger; otherwise kill the process group, `entire session stop <id>`, `git reset --hard` + `git clean -fdx` inside the disposable worktree only, hash the Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/.../<sid>.jsonl`) into the bundle as evidence of the abandoned attempt, write an `abandoned` ledger entry, and start attempt 2 with a **new nonce**. Long-lived in-place sessions (Immunologist refinement, orphan recovery) use `entire session resume <branch>` plus `claude -p --resume <sid>` (spike N7).
- **L3 (wrong fix in production).** Reverting is git (`git revert -m 1` → PR → expedited gates → merge), not Entire. Because audit check C4 requires a checkpoint for **every** commit in W, reverts, L5 configuration treatments and eval-augment commits run inside a templated **headless notary session**: a Claude Code session whose prompt contains the nonce and performs exactly that operation.

### (b) Audit check C4 and the Archivist's Intent Record

**C4/C5**, for every commit in W on protected branches plus attempt refs:

1. Require both the `Kintsugi-*` trailers and an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer.
2. The ref `refs/entire/checkpoints/<id[-2:]>/<id>` must exist on origin. Offline mode reads a `git bundle` of these refs.
3. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`: `files_touched` must cover the files in the diff.
4. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript`: the nonce must appear verbatim and not on a redacted line.
5. Cross-check: `entire why <file>:<line> --json` on sampled changed lines names the same checkpoint and commit.
6. **C5:** the session's first user message, canonicalised and SHA-256'd, equals `Kintsugi-Prompt`.

**Intent Record:** `entire graph search` → `git blame` → resolve the checkpoint two independent ways (`entire why --json` and the commit trailer; they must agree) → read the transcript → select the turn(s) whose Edit/Write tool calls touched the blamed file (the "Intent" field is ignored: it shows the first prompt in the checkpoint's scope) → the Archivist (Opus) writes clauses with verbatim quotes → the Auditor checks every quote against the same transcript bytes, whose SHA-256 is recorded. `git bisect` steps map to checkpoints through trailers; commits without one are labelled `no-checkpoint`. The honeytoken check (§7.2) runs `git grep` over **all** `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` trees.

### (c) Motif engine on entire-graph v0.4.0 (Python)

Python relations: `CALLS`, `ASYNC_CALLS`, `CONSTRUCTS`, `CONTAINS`, `DATA_FLOWS`, `DEFINES`, `IMPORTS`, `EXTENDS`, `INHERITS`, `OVERRIDES`, `PARAM_TYPE`, `RETURNS_TYPE`, `USES_TYPE`, `HANDLES_GRAPHQL`, plus the heuristic relations of the `full` profile (`HTTP_CALLS`, `HANDLES_TOOL`, `TESTS`, `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`). There is no `READS_FIELD`, `WRITES_FIELD`, `ACCESSES` or `IMPLEMENTS` for Python.

- **Motif v1.0:** nodes `R[is_retry_wrapper]`, `Enc` (enclosing function), `F` (the retried scope: nested function, lambda, or the decorated function itself), `S[has_mutable_accumulator]`; edges `[Enc,R,CALLS]`, `[Enc,F,CONTAINS]`, **`[F,S,CONSTRUCTS]`**.
- **Motif v1.1** adds `T[is_side_effecting]` and `[F,T,CALLS*]`, where `CALLS*` is a derived transitive-closure relation computed before VF2 matching (VF2 matches edges exactly).
- **`has_mutable_accumulator`:** `entire graph def S` (fields and methods) plus a deterministic stdlib `ast` scan for list/dict/set fields mutated in methods; Haiku decides only when the scan is inconclusive, and its verdict is cached by (symbol, blob SHA).
- **`is_side_effecting`:** `CALLS*` reaches a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an `HTTP_CALLS` POST/PUT/DELETE.
- Validation is unchanged: match before the fix, no match after it, precision ≥ 0.9 on the healthy fleet. The snapshot record schema is pinned with golden files (A9).

### (d) `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0` everywhere

- Build commits: `.claude/settings.json` `env` block and the CLAUDE.md commit rules.
- Runtime: one subprocess gateway, `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py`, builds every child environment from an allowlist and forces `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_EDITOR=true`, with timeouts and process-tree termination (root first, so a killed `git commit` aborts instead of completing without a trailer). An architecture test and a ruff banned-API rule forbid `subprocess` anywhere else.
- Headless sessions get the environment from the gateway plus `--settings` (which also sets commit attribution to `""`).
- Every commit is verified afterwards (trailer + checkpoint ref). On failure the activity fails, the disposable worktree is reset and nothing is pushed.
- Entire 0.11.4 and entire-graph 0.4.0 are pinned; a contract test runs the hook on a scratch repo under a timeout to catch regressions.

### (e) Further reconciliations

1. **Redaction vs. the proofs (critical, spike N1).** Entire redacts secret-looking lines. A hex nonce or random-looking honeytoken could be blanked: C4 would fail and, worse, C6's "0 honeytoken hits" would pass trivially. Nonces and honeytokens are therefore **passphrase-formatted**; Stage 2 adds a byte-exact prompt round-trip test and a **positive control** proving C6 finds a planted honeytoken.
2. **Parallel Surgeons (N5).** K concurrent sessions in K worktrees: each commit must link to its own session.
3. **Ref syncing.** Checkpoint refs are pushed explicitly after each commit and again after finalize; audit clones fetch `refs/entire/*`.
4. **Public transcripts.** Checkpoint transcripts are pushed with the code: add redaction rules for Anthropic and neatlogs key patterns and a secret scan of checkpoint trees before every push (N6).
5. **Platform.** gVisor (§5.10) needs Linux: the runtime for Stage 3+ and the autonomy run lives in WSL2 Ubuntu (ruling D2). The 24 h run is never launched from inside the Claude desktop app.
6. **No co-author trailers.** The orchestrator's commit validator rejects `Co-authored-by:`; headless sessions get commit attribution set to `""`.

## 3. Architect rulings D1–D8

| # | Decision | Ruling |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | W length and T0 | Deferred to the Stage 8 go/no-go gate, once the C1–C14 mutation checks are green. |
| D2 | Runtime platform | Stages 1–2 stay cross-platform through `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py` so local Windows execution works. Prepare WSL2 Ubuntu + Docker/gVisor for Stage 3+ and the autonomy run. |
| D3 | Repo layout | Build the hosts (`hosts/ledger`, `hosts/scout`, `hosts/triage`), the antibody library (`antibodies/`) and the sabotage log (`sabotage-log/`) inside the `kintsugi-omega` monorepo first, so `suryaprasanthcse/kintsugi-omega` is self-contained and runnable from a single clone. Remote repo adapters are configurable once the GitHub token is provided. |
| D4 | Commit identity | `Surya Prasanth R <suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com>` is the sole git author and committer on all commits. Never a bot contributor, never `Co-authored-by:`. Machine origin is proven by Ed25519 signatures (`.kintsugi/attest.pub`), `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers and `Kintsugi-*` trailers. |
| D5 | Ledger location | An unprotected, append-only `ledger` branch for ledger entries and anchors. |
| D6 | Temporal deployment | Implement both the deterministic `sqlite_fsm.py` WAL state machine and the Temporal workflow/activity definitions, using the single-binary Temporal CLI dev server or Docker Compose when started in Stage 5. |
| D7 | Headless Claude billing | The existing Claude Code login for Stage 2 headless spikes; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with a hard daily dollar cap in `kintsugi/sandbox/llm_proxy.py` and `kintsugi/econ/governor.py` from Stage 3/6. |
| D8 | Parallel build lanes | Approved where safe, provided every commit is made cleanly with `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`, carries a verified `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, and credits lines accurately. |

## 4. Stages

"Rehearsal" means an unsealed, clearly labelled practice run before T0.

### Stage 1 — Foundation and deterministic cores (no credentials)

- **Builds:** `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`, ruff, pyright, `Makefile` (judge, audit, demo, fleet-up/down, check), `.github/workflows/omega-ci.yml`, `kintsugi/cli.py`, `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py`, `kintsugi/proof/{canonical,ledger,sealed,attest,bundle}.py`, `kintsugi/stats/{mcnemar,sprt,power,holm,wilson,bootstrap}.py`, `kintsugi/econ/{governor,wright}.py`, `kintsugi/memory/{antibody,motif}.py`, `kintsugi/control/states.py`, `schemas/E1–E6`, `.kintsugi/protected_paths.yaml`.
- **Commits (~7):** scaffold + plan · proc gateway · proof primitives · stats · econ · memory/motif core · state machine, schemas, protected paths.
- **Verified by:** SPRT boundaries 2.890/−2.251, steps +0.6931/−0.0660, accept after 35 clean runs, reject at n=8 (LLR 3.268), accept at n=46 (LLR −2.275); Connor n=34; McNemar b=26, c=1 → p≈2.09e-7; governor reproduces §6.2 (Pool $71.70, Cap/B $12.40) and §6.8 (B $4.83, T1 $2.34, GM 78.6%); Wright fit recovers b; RFC 8785 vectors; ledger tamper detected at the exact seq; commit-reveal and Ed25519 round-trip; property test: every state path terminates. Spike N3 is checked on the first commit.
- **Invariants:** model-level I3; I4 formulas; I1/I2/I7 primitives. **Cascade/proof:** SPRT core (L3), L5 math, building blocks for C1, C3, C6.

### Stage 2 — Entire, graph, git and attestation layer + headless spikes

- **Builds:** `kintsugi/memory/{entire,graph}.py` (every subcommand, JSON adapters, golden fixtures), `kintsugi/sandbox/worktree.py`, `kintsugi/crew/claude_session.py` (`claude -p --output-format stream-json --allowedTools … --settings …`, nonce injection, cost and transcript capture), `kintsugi/proof/{commit,redaction}.py`, `tests/contract/test_entire_*.py`.
- **Spikes (contract tests on scratch repos):** A1/N2 (does Entire link a commit made after `claude -p` exits?), N1 (redaction vs nonce/honeytoken/prompt formats), N5 (three concurrent worktrees), A14 (`kill -9` mid-session), N4 (hooks inside worktrees), A9 (snapshot schema).
- **Commits:** ~6. **Verified by:** C4/C5 pass on real checkpoints and fail on mutated ones; `entire why` agrees with the trailer mapping; the C6 positive control finds a planted honeytoken.
- **Invariants:** I2 machinery; I6 detectability; I5 transcript-scan tooling. **Cascade/proof:** L1 attempt checkpoints, L2 abandoned-session handling, C2–C6.

### Stage 3 — Fleet: Ledger, Scout, Triage + sandbox and proxies (monorepo, D3)

- **Builds:** `hosts/ledger` (`ReconcileSession`, `run_reconcile`, `util/retry.py`, tools `parse_invoice`, `lookup_vendor` with a default argument, `fx_rate`, side-effecting `post_journal_entry`, `fmt_amount`; runtime with auto-deploy from main; 120-invoice generator 80/40; exact-match grader; `test_resume_after_partial_batch`), `hosts/scout` (BM25 frozen corpus; the disclosed look-alike per-attempt scratch buffer; 40/20), `hosts/triage` (mock GitHub, `config/routing.yaml`, mixed-language issues; 70/30), `kintsugi/sandbox/{runner,llm_proxy,chaos_proxy,cassette}.py`, age-encrypted holdouts, `.kintsugi/holdout.sha256`, per-host CI and a reusable G7 workflow, `grader.verdict` spans. WSL2 + Docker + gVisor integration (D2). Remote repo adapters stay configurable (D3).
- **Commits:** ~12. **Verified by:** baselines at 3 seeds ≥ SLO with Wilson CI; Ledger handles 8% background 429s with no duplicate lines; deterministic cassette replay; chaos proxy identical per seed; proxy enforces budgets and meters cost within 1%; sandbox blocks non-allowlisted egress; `neatlogs doctor --probe`; holdout canary strings for leak scans.
- **Invariants:** I5 (encryption), I4 (proxy caps). **Cascade/proof:** code shapes for S‑17 (L0), S‑19 targets (L4), the Scout look-alike (L3), Triage Pilot on Haiku (L5).

### Stage 4 — Senses: neatlogs, receptors, ingress, poller, Fixes

- **Builds:** `kintsugi/senses/{neatlogs_api,detections,ingress,poller,tags,fixes_mcp}.py`, receptors R‑001…R‑007 per host, SQLite dedupe store, webhook registration. **Spikes:** A3–A7, A11–A13.
- **Commits:** ~6. **Verified by:** contract tests against the pinned OpenAPI; duplicate events dropped with 200; ingress answers within 2 s; poller recovers hits during a simulated outage; replayed deliveries suppressed; I7 completeness function on fixtures.

- **Builds:** `kintsugi/control/workflows.py` (8 workflows), `activities.py` (all §5.3.2 activities with timeouts, heartbeats, retries, idempotency keys), `worker.py` (separate crew, Surgeon, senses pools), `sqlite_fsm.py` (§5.4 resume algorithm, single-writer socket), `watchdog.py` (supervision, health checks, authenticated chaos API, dead-man switch).

- **Invariants:** I3, I1 ordering. **Cascade/proof:** L2, L4 signal path, T8.

### Stage 6 — Crew, primary incident loop, gates G0–G7, ship (L0, L1, L4)

- **Builds:** `kintsugi/crew/{sentinel,pathologist,archivist,coordinator,surgeon,auditor}.py` with hashed prompt templates, `kintsugi/senses/{signature,drift}.py`, `kintsugi/gates/g0…g7`, context manifests, `kintsugi/control/ship.py` (issues, PRs with the E.4 receipt, merges), the protected-path pre-commit hook, `.github/workflows/g7-gates.yml` (holdout key in an Actions secret; logs print aggregates only).
- **Commits:** ~12. **Verified by a full Ledger rehearsal:** G0 fails 3/3 → Intent Record with verified quotes → three parallel Surgeons, each with a checkpoint → round 1 fails and is rewound → round 2 → pre-registered dispute experiment → ship → G7 green → merge. **Negative tests:** protected-path edits blocked twice; diffs over 120 lines blocked; new outbound network calls blocked; zero holdout leaks across crew spans and transcripts; the Auditor never sees Surgeon output; G6 stops a round when the budget is spent. **L4 drill:** a mid-round drift push → rebase → reverify record.
- **Invariants:** I1, I3, I5. **Cascade/proof:** L0, L1, L4; C2–C5, C7; T2, T5.

### Stage 7 — Canary, antibodies, motif engine, vaccination, quarantine (L3)

- **Builds:** `kintsugi/gates/canary.py`, `kintsugi/control/revert.py`, `kintsugi/memory/{motif,predicates,library,contrastive}.py`, `kintsugi/crew/immunologist.py` (synthesis, receptor generate/preview/create/activate, backfill, maturation, vaccination, quarantine, refinement), the `antibodies/` library in the monorepo (D3), the trace-to-test eval-augment path.
- **Commits:** ~10. **Verified by:** motif validation (match before, not after, precision ≥ 0.9); induced-trigger rule; receptor preview precision ≥ 0.9; a backfill job completes; L3 rehearsal (Scout canary reject → revert PR → reverse canary → `pause_antibody` → comments on open PRs → QUARANTINED with the receptor still active); contrastive learner separates 3 positives from Scout; v1.1 motif excludes Scout; consistent lineage; secondary responses measured far cheaper than primary.
- **Cascade/proof:** L3, L0 steps 11–14, S5, C11, T9.

### Stage 8 — Proof plane: Saboteur, sealing, ledger anchors, `kintsugi audit`

Attempt commits stay reachable (never garbage-collected) and audit checks C2–C5 can verify them.
- **L2 (process killed mid-session).** A headless session killed before its Stop hook has no shadow branch and no checkpoint (A14). Recovery: adopt a commit whose nonce matches the ledger; otherwise kill the process group, `entire session stop <id>`, `git reset --hard` + `git clean -fdx` inside the disposable worktree only, hash the Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/.../<sid>.jsonl`) into the bundle as evidence of the abandoned attempt, write an `abandoned` ledger entry, and start attempt 2 with a **new nonce**. Long-lived in-place sessions (Immunologist refinement, orphan recovery) use `entire session resume <branch>` plus `claude -p --resume <sid>` (spike N7).
- **L3 (wrong fix in production).** Reverting is git (`git revert -m 1` → PR → expedited gates → merge), not Entire. Because audit check C4 requires a checkpoint for **every** commit in W, reverts, L5 configuration treatments and eval-augment commits run inside a templated **headless notary session**: a Claude Code session whose prompt contains the nonce and performs exactly that operation.

### (b) Audit check C4 and the Archivist's Intent Record

**C4/C5**, for every commit in W on protected branches plus attempt refs:

1. Require both the `Kintsugi-*` trailers and an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer.
2. The ref `refs/entire/checkpoints/<id[-2:]>/<id>` must exist on origin. Offline mode reads a `git bundle` of these refs.
3. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`: `files_touched` must cover the files in the diff.
4. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript`: the nonce must appear verbatim and not on a redacted line.
5. Cross-check: `entire why <file>:<line> --json` on sampled changed lines names the same checkpoint and commit.
6. **C5:** the session's first user message, canonicalised and SHA-256'd, equals `Kintsugi-Prompt`.

**Intent Record:** `entire graph search` → `git blame` → resolve the checkpoint two independent ways (`entire why --json` and the commit trailer; they must agree) → read the transcript → select the turn(s) whose Edit/Write tool calls touched the blamed file (the "Intent" field is ignored: it shows the first prompt in the checkpoint's scope) → the Archivist (Opus) writes clauses with verbatim quotes → the Auditor checks every quote against the same transcript bytes, whose SHA-256 is recorded. `git bisect` steps map to checkpoints through trailers; commits without one are labelled `no-checkpoint`. The honeytoken check (§7.2) runs `git grep` over **all** `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` trees.

### (c) Motif engine on entire-graph v0.4.0 (Python)

Python relations: `CALLS`, `ASYNC_CALLS`, `CONSTRUCTS`, `CONTAINS`, `DATA_FLOWS`, `DEFINES`, `IMPORTS`, `EXTENDS`, `INHERITS`, `OVERRIDES`, `PARAM_TYPE`, `RETURNS_TYPE`, `USES_TYPE`, `HANDLES_GRAPHQL`, plus the heuristic relations of the `full` profile (`HTTP_CALLS`, `HANDLES_TOOL`, `TESTS`, `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`). There is no `READS_FIELD`, `WRITES_FIELD`, `ACCESSES` or `IMPLEMENTS` for Python.

- **Motif v1.0:** nodes `R[is_retry_wrapper]`, `Enc` (enclosing function), `F` (the retried scope: nested function, lambda, or the decorated function itself), `S[has_mutable_accumulator]`; edges `[Enc,R,CALLS]`, `[Enc,F,CONTAINS]`, **`[F,S,CONSTRUCTS]`**.
- **Motif v1.1** adds `T[is_side_effecting]` and `[F,T,CALLS*]`, where `CALLS*` is a derived transitive-closure relation computed before VF2 matching (VF2 matches edges exactly).
- **`has_mutable_accumulator`:** `entire graph def S` (fields and methods) plus a deterministic stdlib `ast` scan for list/dict/set fields mutated in methods; Haiku decides only when the scan is inconclusive, and its verdict is cached by (symbol, blob SHA).
- **`is_side_effecting`:** `CALLS*` reaches a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an `HTTP_CALLS` POST/PUT/DELETE.
- Validation is unchanged: match before the fix, no match after it, precision ≥ 0.9 on the healthy fleet. The snapshot record schema is pinned with golden files (A9).

### (d) `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0` everywhere

- Build commits: `.claude/settings.json` `env` block and the CLAUDE.md commit rules.
- Runtime: one subprocess gateway, `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py`, builds every child environment from an allowlist and forces `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_EDITOR=true`, with timeouts and process-tree termination (root first, so a killed `git commit` aborts instead of completing without a trailer). An architecture test and a ruff banned-API rule forbid `subprocess` anywhere else.
- Headless sessions get the environment from the gateway plus `--settings` (which also sets commit attribution to `""`).
- Every commit is verified afterwards (trailer + checkpoint ref). On failure the activity fails, the disposable worktree is reset and nothing is pushed.
- Entire 0.11.4 and entire-graph 0.4.0 are pinned; a contract test runs the hook on a scratch repo under a timeout to catch regressions.

### (e) Further reconciliations

1. **Redaction vs. the proofs (critical, spike N1).** Entire redacts secret-looking lines. A hex nonce or random-looking honeytoken could be blanked: C4 would fail and, worse, C6's "0 honeytoken hits" would pass trivially. Nonces and honeytokens are therefore **passphrase-formatted**; Stage 2 adds a byte-exact prompt round-trip test and a **positive control** proving C6 finds a planted honeytoken.
2. **Parallel Surgeons (N5).** K concurrent sessions in K worktrees: each commit must link to its own session.
3. **Ref syncing.** Checkpoint refs are pushed explicitly after each commit and again after finalize; audit clones fetch `refs/entire/*`.
4. **Public transcripts.** Checkpoint transcripts are pushed with the code: add redaction rules for Anthropic and neatlogs key patterns and a secret scan of checkpoint trees before every push (N6).
5. **Platform.** gVisor (§5.10) needs Linux: the runtime for Stage 3+ and the autonomy run lives in WSL2 Ubuntu (ruling D2). The 24 h run is never launched from inside the Claude desktop app.
6. **No co-author trailers.** The orchestrator's commit validator rejects `Co-authored-by:`; headless sessions get commit attribution set to `""`.

"""Motif engine on fleet-shaped fixture graphs: the full L3 learning story of spec §6.5–§6.7."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import networkx as nx
import pytest

from kintsugi.memory import motif as m
from kintsugi.memory.antibody import MotifSpec


def _host(
    *,
    retried_scope_constructs: bool,
    scope_side_effect: bool,
    accumulator_cls: str = "ReconcileSession",
    hoisted: bool = False,
    dedupe_guard: bool = False,
) -> nx.DiGraph:
    """A host shaped like Ledger: run_reconcile → retry_with_backoff(attempt) with a session."""
    symbols = [
        m.Symbol("run", "function", "run_reconcile"),
        m.Symbol("retry", "function", "retry_with_backoff"),
        m.Symbol("attempt", "function", "attempt"),
        m.Symbol("session", "class", accumulator_cls, attrs={"mutable_accumulator": True}),
        m.Symbol("helper", "function", "_post_lines"),
        m.Symbol("tool", "function", "post_or_fetch", attrs={"side_effect": scope_side_effect}),
        m.Symbol("fx", "function", "fx_rate"),
        m.Symbol("guard", "function", "dedupe_guard", attrs={"dedupe_guard": True}),
    ]
    relations = [
        m.Relation("run", "retry", "CALLS"),
        m.Relation("run", "attempt", "CONTAINS"),
        m.Relation("attempt", "helper", "CALLS"),
        m.Relation("helper", "tool", "CALLS"),
        m.Relation("attempt", "fx", "CALLS"),
        m.Relation("attempt", "requests.post", "CALLS"),  # external: skipped and counted
    ]
    if retried_scope_constructs:
        relations.append(m.Relation("attempt", "session", "CONSTRUCTS"))
    if hoisted:
        relations.append(m.Relation("run", "session", "CONSTRUCTS"))
    if dedupe_guard:
        relations.append(m.Relation("attempt", "guard", "CALLS"))
    graph = m.build_graph(symbols, relations)
    m.add_transitive_calls(graph)
    return graph


LEDGER_BEFORE = _host(retried_scope_constructs=True, scope_side_effect=True)
LEDGER_AFTER = _host(retried_scope_constructs=False, scope_side_effect=True, hoisted=True)

    retried_scope_constructs=True, scope_side_effect=False, accumulator_cls="ScratchBuffer"
)

}
MOTIF_V1_0 = MotifSpec.model_validate(_CORE)

        "nodes": {**_CORE["nodes"], "T": {"kind": "function", "pred": ["is_side_effecting"]}},

)
